headline: High risk: shared Replit filesystem plus broad shell/write access can leak secrets and cascade errors when paired with Argo Workflows' API-driven automation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no documented direct message channel, but B can read/write Repl workspace files and A can operate on artifacts/parameters via APIs. If A’s outputs are copied into shared files, B could treat them as instructions. This is a limited, user-mediated bridge rather than a default direct injection path.
conditions: IF A’s workflow outputs are written into a Repl workspace file that B later reads as prompt text
IF the operator manually copies A-generated content into B’s task context
mitigations: Keep A outputs in a separate, read-only artifact store
Use a strict file naming convention for data vs instructions
Add a one-line human review before B consumes A outputs
Disable automatic ingestion of workspace files into prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration and has broad filesystem and network egress. A handles artifacts and parameters and can call APIs. If A’s artifacts or parameters include sensitive data and are placed in the shared Repl workspace, B can read them and potentially exfiltrate them through broad egress. The shared workspace makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF A writes artifacts or parameters containing secrets into the shared Repl workspace
IF B is allowed to read those files before redaction
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Redact artifacts before handing them to B
Restrict B’s network egress to allowlisted destinations
Separate workspaces per agent
Add a pre-transfer scan for secrets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem and modify_git_state in a persistent shared Repl filesystem; A can interact with APIs and produce artifacts that may be materialized into the same workspace. That creates overlapping mutable-state access and possible git/workspace races. A lacks local write capability, so this is not the highest tier, but the shared mutable surface is real.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are materialized into the same Repl workspace that B edits
IF B commits or rewrites git state while A-triggered jobs are still producing artifacts
mitigations: Use per-agent branches or worktrees
Lock the workspace during writes
Serialize git operations through one operator
Keep A outputs outside the git checkout
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces artifacts/parameters and B can act on files, shell commands, and git state. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or deployments. A does not have direct action authority here, but B’s downstream power makes unverified handoff risky in default workflows.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated artifacts as ground truth without validation
IF B uses A-produced parameters to edit code or deployment config
mitigations: Require a validation step before B acts on A outputs
Add schema checks for A artifacts
Have a human approve deployment-affecting changes
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs
requires-engineering: enforce typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Replit environment, while A is an open-source workflow engine that can process artifacts and parameters. If regulated data such as secrets or sensitive deployment material flows from A into B’s Repl workspace, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s Replit workspace or secrets store
IF the operator requires a residency or retention policy that differs between the two environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Replit workspace
Document data-class handling for each agent
Use separate retention policies per data class
Review vendor terms before processing sensitive data
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
